name: voice-forge
desc: Free, open-source TTS studio for Windows — local neural voices, batch narration, audiobook export. 100 MB portable, offline, MIT, no cloud.
features: ✅ **Local neural voices** — Piper-class ONNX models speak on your machine with no API keys
✅ **Batch narration** — feed a folder of text files or a CSV and get one audio file per line
✅ **Audiobook export** — long text split into numbered chapters with silence between them
✅ **Pause and emphasis controls** — comma pauses, sentence gaps and speed per voice tuned in the panel
✅ **Voice audition shelf** — ten voices compared on the same sentence before committing to a read
✅ **WAV and MP3 out** — raw audio for editing or encoded files ready to publish
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime bundled, voices download separately, offline after that, MIT
compare: | Price | **Free, MIT** | Paid subscription | Freeware | Free, OSS |
| Text stays local | **Yes** | Uploaded | Yes | Yes
| Batch CSV narration | **Yes** | API only | Partial | Scripted |
| Audiobook chapter export | **Yes** | No | No | No |
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Browser | Installer | Python env
faqQ: free text to speech for Windows that works offline?
faqA: Cloud voices bill per character and the text leaves your machine, while old offline voices still sound robotic. voice-forge runs neural TTS models locally, narrates whole folders in batch and exports chaptered audiobooks. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, unlimited characters, no account needed.
s1: Dark studio (#121418, magenta #E879F9): text editor left with a highlighted pause marker, voice shelf right with ten audition rows, waveform strip at bottom.
s2: Batch narration: CSV with 240 rows mapped to output names, progress at 132 files, per-row status lights, ETA chip reading 18 minutes.
s3: Audiobook export: chapter list auto-split on headings, silence gap stepper at 1.2 s, bitrate dropdown, toast reading 24 chapter files written.
